title: Telephony
description: How a session reaches the phone network, referenced from the resolved session config's telephony property. Kept in its own file so the resolved config stays under its size cap.

Telephony.description: How a session reaches the phone network, referenced from the resolved session config's telephony property. On the telephony channel the session is the phone call. On any other channel phones join only when phoneGuests says so: each call placed into the session brings one phone guest, voice only, and the channel's own tuning still decides how the agent behaves. A session that takes no phone keeps no telephony block, so resolution drops the tenant's block from every other session. The phone number a call goes to is never part of this block or of any stored document: it is given once, to the control plane route that places the call, and the person on the line joins under an opaque participant id the control plane mints. A phone call cannot be end-to-end encrypted, because the media server's SIP bridge decodes every frame between the phone network and the room, and a recorded session a phone can join needs the agent to tell the person on the line; both are cross-field rules.

trunk.description: The operator's SIP trunk that carries the call, named by its key in the control plane's trunk table, which binds it to one provider's address, the numbers calls are placed from and the credentials, all of them secret:// references. It is the tenant's phone line, set in the tenant's configuration, because a trunk carries that tenant's numbers and bill; a session never states an address or a credential, and a session override cannot name a trunk. Absent: the tenant has no phone line, so no call can be placed into the session.

phoneGuests.description: Whether people may join a session on another channel by phone, which the session creator decides, since each phone costs a call and hears the session. off: no phone joins. dial_out: the control plane may call phones into the session on the tenant's trunk. dial_in: a person may phone one of the trunk's meeting numbers and join the running session, admitted by dialIn.callerCheck. both: dial_out and dial_in. Must be off on the telephony channel, where the session is the call itself.

ringingTimeoutSeconds.description: How long an outbound call rings before it is given up.

maxCallDurationSeconds.description: The longest a phone call in this session lasts before the media server hangs it up, so a call nobody ends does not run up the provider bill.

recordingNotice.description: What the agent says about recording each time a phone in the session is answered, before anything else and without being interruptible, because a person on a phone sees no recording indicator. always: it says the call is recorded when recording is on and that it is not when recording is off. when_recorded: it says so only when recording is on and says nothing about it otherwise. Whether the session is recorded is recording.enabled, which the session creator sets; recording still needs its consent artifact.

DialIn.description: How a person who phones one of the trunk's meeting numbers is admitted to a session whose phoneGuests is dial_in or both; stating it in any other session is a cross-field error. The meeting PIN is minted by the control plane, unique among running sessions and never part of this block or of any stored document, because the document is hashed, stored and handed to every joiner; the numbers a caller check allows are given to their own control plane route and stored only as keyed hashes.

callerCheck.description: Who a dial-in call admits. pin: anyone who keys in the meeting PIN. pin_and_number: the meeting PIN and a calling number on the session's allowlist. number: a calling number on the session's allowlist, without a PIN; a number allowed in more than one running session is asked for the PIN rather than guessed. A withheld calling number fails every number check.
